Reference Issues/PRs
Related to https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/26267
Addresses https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/26267#discussion_r1206838572


#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.
- Renames `DistanceMetric-->DistanceMetric64` in line with `DistanceMetric32`
- Adds `DistanceMetric` as an abstract base class for `DistanceMetric{32, 64}`
- Adds a general `get_metric` method to `DistanceMetric` which accepts a `dtype` argument to decide on metric specialization internally, without requiring explicit use of `DistanceMetric{32, 64}.get_metric`

Somewhat optional:

A recap of a few goals established so far in this PR:

1. We need to ensure backwards compatibility of `{KD, Ball}Tree`. That is to say, `{KD, Ball}Tree64` should be exposed as `{KD, Ball}Tree`.
2. We need to find a nice way allowing the user to grab the correct type-specialized tree.
3. We should be consistent between `DistanceMetric` and `{KD, Ball}Tree`. If we make a change here, we ought to propagate it to `DistanceMetric`.
4. We should obfuscate type-specialization of the `{KD, Ball}Tree` objects from the user (e.g. via boxing as suggested by @jjerphan).

While the proposed box strategy would accomplish these goals, propagating it `DistanceMetric` may be a bit suboptimal. We have a lot of very tight calls to `*.dist` which would incur additional indirection overhead. We could unbox it and type-specialize it at the call site but that would make code much more complex.

Note that @thomasjpfan does not consider this necessary, and after discussing it with him I agree. For me, it would be _nice_, but we already do not do it for `DistanceMetric` and the presence of type information (e.g. this obj is exactly `{KD, Ball}Tree{32, 64}`) _can_ actually be helpful to the user. I am +0 to it, and would not hold up this work just to ensure it.

With that being said, if we drop criterion 4 we can effectively borrow what `DistanceMetric` does as an alternative solution.

We can begin an API deprecation to move users away from constructing trees directly, and instead using a factory method (similar to `DistanceMetric.get_metric`). Then, later, we can separate `{KD, Ball}Tree` from `{KD, Ball}Tree64`. Thus we would:
1. Add a `FutureWarning` to `BinaryTree.__init__` to begin deprecation
2. Introduce `get_tree(...)` to `{KD, Ball}Tree64` with the same signature of `BinaryTree.__init__`, which is in charge of constructing the type-specialized trees directly.
3. Suppress the `FutureWarning` using a context manager in `{KD, Ball}Tree64.get_tree`.
4. **Complete the deprecation** by introducing a separate `{KD, Ball}Tree` into the hierarchy which comes with the same `get_tree` method and fully remove the `FutureWarning` from `{KD, Ball}Tree{32, 64}` since they should no longer be directly constructed.

At the end, the expected API is:
```python
from sklearn.neighbors import KDTree

# Data
X = ...

# tree is thus an instance of KDTree{32, 64} based on X.dtype
tree = KDTree.get_tree(X, ...)
```

In the next PR we will introduce the deprecation:
> 1. Add a `FutureWarning` to `BinaryTree.__init__` to begin deprecation
> 2. Introduce `get_tree(...)` to `{KD, Ball}Tree64` with the same signature of `BinaryTree.__init__`, which is in charge of constructing the type-specialized trees directly.
> 3. Suppress the `FutureWarning` using a context manager in `{KD, Ball}Tree64.get_tree`

Towards https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/23958

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.
This simplifies the original implementation of `PairwiseDistance` by @jjerphan, with the following differences:
- `PairwiseDistance{32,64}` doesn't subclass `BaseDistancesReduction{32,64}` anymore.
- This allows to add `_parallel_on_{X,Y}` methods to `PairwiseDistance{32,64}`, since these methods are decorated with `@final` in `BaseBaseDistancesReduction{32,64}` and thus can't be overwritten.
- This also remove the chunk computing mechanism, by considering only the case `chunk_size = 1`, as proposed by @ogrisel in [this comment](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/23958#issuecomment-1280517094).
- This doesn't implement the Euclidean specialization yet to make benchmarks simpler.

Following [this benchmark](https://gist.github.com/Vincent-Maladiere/67e9efa5fc02cbe48e052b97372115af), we found that this PR yields a significant performance regression when `n_jobs = 1` and an improvement when `n_jobs > 1`, for both euclidean and manhattan distances:

![euclidean](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18560386/216777160-a48b1578-d890-464a-8a92-ffe0ca707134.png)

![manhattan](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18560386/216777169-b6686780-ae12-4da7-be50-b5965c5bd7aa.png)

#### Any other comments?

As suggested by @jjerphan, decorating `DistanceMetric` subclasses with `@final` could alleviate some of the overhead and make this implementation competitive with `main` when `n_jobs=1`.
